entries.test: Marcus's earlier newsletter warnings and public evidence of deteriorating web quality, widespread misinformation, and increased cyberscams would establish whether the named harms occurred.
entries.note: The broad wording still identifies observable harms.

entries.test: Public evidence that each named harm continued despite optimistic AI promotion would establish the claim's plain reading.
entries.note: The loaded adjective does not erase the factual assertion that the harms persisted.

entries.test: The December 2022 WIRED prediction and dated records of chatbot-related deaths would establish whether the first such death occurred in 2023.
entries.note: This is a retrospective claim of predictive success; 'first' requires examining earlier cases too.

entries.test: Reporting and case records available by April 2023 would establish whether a death associated with chatbot use had occurred and whether causal attribution remained uncertain.
entries.note: Association is asserted; proven causation is expressly qualified.

entries.test: Public reporting published by January 15, 2026 would establish whether several chatbot-associated deaths had been reported, including both suicide and murder.
entries.note: The claim concerns reported associations, not established causation.

entries.test: Court filings and public docket records would establish whether OpenAI faced at least eight wrongful death lawsuits involving deceased ChatGPT users on January 15, 2026.
entries.note: Count wrongful death lawsuits, not all lawsuits alleging chatbot harms.

entries.test: Dated public case records and reporting would establish whether chatbot-associated deaths were increasing in frequency or severity approaching publication.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies a plain reading of worsening death-related harms.
The recommendation to give children special concern is a value judgment.
'Apparently' qualifies the alleged induction of delusions; Marcus does not firmly assert that causal relationship.
The proposition drops 'increasingly convinced,' making the judgment more categorical. Whether AI is a net step forward for humanity depends on evaluative standards.
